purpose: Quality reference for upgrading the 850-word database. Confirmed-core entries are directly supported by recovered historical project material; reconstructed-core entries are newly standardized from the same English-thinking framework and must remain reviewable.

items.core_image: A bridge / connector that places the subject at an identity, location, or state.
items.core_logic: BE does not launch an action; it connects the subject to what situation it is in.
meaning_growth: foundation for be + doing and be + done

confusions.difference: Action verbs encode the action itself; BE locates/connects the subject to a state or information.

items.card_metaphor: A 3D bridge connecting the subject to three destinations: identity, location and state.

items.core_image: A finger or arrow precisely targeting a point.
items.core_logic: AT compresses a target into a point and directs attention/action toward that point.
meaning_growth: target of an action or attention

confusions.difference: AT conceptualizes a point; ON a surface/contact relation; IN a containing region.

items.card_metaphor: A bright target point with an arrow/finger locking onto it.

items.core_image: Two surfaces in contact / something attached to a surface or connection.
items.core_logic: ON builds a contact or connected relation that can extend from physical surfaces to active connections and attached states.

confusions.difference: ON suggests contact/connection; OFF suggests detachment/disconnection.

items.card_metaphor: Two clean 3D surfaces snapping into contact, with a connected/active branch.

items.core_image: An object enclosed by a three-dimensional container or surrounding state.
items.core_logic: IN conceptualizes something as being within the bounds of a containing region, physical or abstract.

confusions.difference: IN gives the target volume/boundaries; ON gives surface contact; AT reduces it to a point.

items.card_metaphor: A transparent 3D container enclosing an object; branches show room, time and emotion containers.

items.core_image: An arrow oriented toward a destination or goal.
items.core_logic: TO encodes target-directed orientation: something is pointed, transferred or conceptually directed toward a goal.

confusions.difference: TO highlights direction/target rather than simply where something already is.

items.card_metaphor: A luminous 3D arrow traveling from origin to a clearly marked target.

items.core_image: Visual information arrives in the eyes/awareness.
items.core_logic: SEE is primarily reception/perception: the image enters awareness without emphasizing deliberate eye movement.

confusions.difference: LOOK is the deliberate turning/directing of the eyes.
WATCH keeps attention on something through time/change.

items.card_metaphor: An object enters a visual field and reaches an eye/awareness node.

items.core_image: The eyes deliberately turn toward a target.
items.core_logic: LOOK is an intentional eye-direction action; another word such as AT often supplies the target.

confusions.difference: SEE receives visual information; LOOK directs the eyes.
WATCH adds sustained attention over a changing process.

items.card_metaphor: A pair of eyes rotates, then a beam points to a target dot.

items.core_image: The eyes stay with a target as it changes over time.
items.core_logic: WATCH means sustained visual attention to a process, movement, or changing scene.

confusions.difference: LOOK directs the eyes; WATCH keeps them engaged over time.

items.card_metaphor: A moving object leaves a short time trail while the eye tracks it continuously.

items.core_image: Something comes into your possession, reach, access, or present state.
items.core_logic: GET is a movement toward acquisition or arrival: from not-having/not-being-there to having/reaching/entering the result.
meaning_growth: come to understand or receive information

confusions.difference: GIVE sends something outward toward another holder; GET is the receiving/acquiring side.

items.card_metaphor: A 3D path moves an object or subject from outside toward a receiving zone, destination, or new-state zone.

items.core_image: A hand takes hold of something and carries it away / into the subject's control.
items.core_logic: TAKE foregrounds actively taking something from its current place or accepting it into one's control, time, responsibility, or experience.
meaning_growth: capture/obtain an instance such as a photo

confusions.difference: PUT moves something to a destination; TAKE removes/accepts it from its current position or into control.
BRING is oriented toward a reference point; TAKE often carries away from the current/reference point.

items.card_metaphor: A hand closes around an object, then a path carries it away; abstract branches turn the object into time/responsibility/photo tokens.

items.core_image: A hand places an object into a chosen position or relation.
items.core_logic: PUT is destination-dependent placement: the action feels incomplete until you know where/into what relation the thing is placed.
meaning_growth: put into a state or arrangement
combine with direction words to specify the placement path
scenes: Put the book on the table.

confusions.difference: PUT sends/places an object into a destination; TAKE removes or takes control of it.

items.card_metaphor: A hand moves a block toward an empty destination socket; direction words change the socket/path.

items.core_image: Something moves out from the current holder toward another person/target.
items.core_logic: GIVE is outward transfer: possession, information, opportunity, or effect moves from source to recipient.
meaning_growth: cause an effect to be received

confusions.difference: GIVE is the source/outgoing side of transfer; GET is the receiving/acquiring side.

items.card_metaphor: An object leaves a source platform and follows an arrow to a recipient platform.

items.core_image: Movement toward the speaker, listener, or active reference point.
items.core_logic: COME is motion toward 'here'—the viewpoint/reference center selected by the conversation.

confusions.difference: COME moves toward the active reference point; GO moves away from it or toward another destination.

items.card_metaphor: A character/object follows a path inward toward a glowing HERE/reference beacon.

items.core_image: Movement away from the current/reference point toward elsewhere.
items.core_logic: GO is motion from 'here' toward another place, path, or state.
meaning_growth: transition into a condition with complements such as go bad / go on

confusions.difference: GO moves away from the reference point; COME moves toward it.

items.card_metaphor: A path leaves a HERE platform and branches toward destinations or new-state zones.

items.core_image: Something is held within the subject's sphere: possession, feature, relation, or accumulated result.
items.core_logic: HAVE places something inside the subject's possession/control/experience sphere; auxiliary HAVE extends this to a result that is now 'held' as completed experience.

confusions.difference: GET emphasizes coming into possession/state; HAVE emphasizes the resulting possession/state already held.

items.card_metaphor: A subject stands inside a transparent possession sphere containing objects/features; a completed-result token is stored in the same sphere.

items.core_image: Perform an act / carry out work without specifying creation of a new product.
items.core_logic: DO foregrounds performing or executing an activity; as an auxiliary it carries grammatical work for questions, negatives and emphasis.

confusions.difference: DO emphasizes performing an activity; MAKE emphasizes producing/creating a result or causing a change.

items.card_metaphor: A workbench shows hands performing an activity; a second branch shows DO as a grammatical support beam carrying NOT/question structure.

items.core_image: Act on materials/situation so that a new result, form, or state comes into existence.
items.core_logic: MAKE is result-producing action: something is created, formed, arranged, or caused to become different.

confusions.difference: MAKE highlights the produced result/change; DO highlights the activity being performed.

items.card_metaphor: Raw pieces enter a small 3D workshop and exit as a formed object/result; an abstract branch changes a state meter.

items.core_image: Detachment: something leaves contact, connection, an active path, or a prior state.
items.core_logic: OFF is the separation/disconnection side of the ON/OFF pair.

confusions.difference: ON maintains contact/connection; OFF breaks or leaves that relation.

items.card_metaphor: Two connected 3D pieces separate; the glow/path switches off as distance opens between them.

items.core_image: Two independent entities are brought into the same scene / relation.
items.core_logic: WITH groups entities inside one shared situation; the exact relation may be accompaniment, instrument, interaction, or opposition.

confusions.difference: TO highlights directed movement/transfer toward a target; WITH places participants together in one relation/scene.

items.root_affix: Historical notes exist in the project, but etymology is auxiliary and should not override the modern shared-scene model.
items.card_metaphor: Two separate 3D pieces slide into one shared scene frame; branches show companion, tool and interaction roles.

items.core_image: A part, quality, content, or element is mentally taken from a larger whole while retaining its relationship to that whole.
items.core_logic: OF links an element back to the whole/source/domain it belongs to or is characterized by.

confusions.difference: OF commonly preserves an internal/constitutive relation; FROM foregrounds source/origin and often separation or transformation.
OF readily expresses part/whole, content and inherent relations; 's often foregrounds possessor association.

items.card_metaphor: A larger 3D whole opens and one labeled part/content piece is lifted out while a glowing tether preserves its relation to the whole.
